question: Out of sample, which removes more of the SPATIAL stable-ground residual: our per-swath along-track drift spline, or DeLong's IDW correction surface?

inputs.role: per-return offsets with every correction term separable, so any combination of routes can be rebuilt from the SAME returns
elevation-cut floodplain mask; stands in for DeLong's 100 m stream buffer
grid geometry (res, origin) for the correction surface

params.name: block_m
params.why: SWEPT, never chosen: held-out blocks smaller than the correlation length let an IDW score its own neighbours, larger ones starve it, so a single value would BE the answer. Excludes no data at any size -- every cell is held out exactly once per size

params.name: folds
params.why: k-fold over whole blocks. Every cell is predicted exactly once from a model that never saw its block; nothing is discarded

params.name: seed
params.why: fixed so the fold assignment reproduces

params.name: radius_m
params.why: coreg.correction_surface's own default and DeLong's 400 m; the honest reach of the interpolation, beyond which it injects error

params.name: slope_max_deg
params.why: DeLong s4.4 'areas with slope >3 deg', verified verbatim in the extracted text. MINE because a published constant has no category here and adopting it was my choice; the value is checkable in the paper

params.name: dz_max_mm
params.why: DeLong's companion cut, 'DoD values >0.7 m in flat areas'. Applied to the RAW d_mm so the identical returns serve every route

params.name: tile
params.why: the tile with a built table; not chosen by its answer

masks.name: stable
masks.defn: in grid, slope <= 3.0 deg, |raw dz| <= 700.0 mm, not floodplain -- DeLong's definition with their stream buffer substituted

columns.route: base = geoid+lateral+swath (shared); ours = base+drift spline; delong = base+IDW correction surface
columns.oos_sd: sd of the held-out stable cell residual, ddof=1, mm
columns.oos_nmad: 1.4826*MAD of the same, mm -- robust twin of oos_sd
columns.|line step|: mean |per-line step| over adjacent pairs in shared cells, mm. The SECOND criterion: a route can buy spatial skill by turning spatial structure into per-line offsets, and skill alone hides that. Lower is better; the base value is what swath alignment already achieved
columns.drift->CS / CS->drift: the two ORDERINGS of the combined mode. Order is not cosmetic: a drift fit on a residual that still holds a spatial field absorbs that field per-line
columns.extrap%: percentage of held-out points lying OUTSIDE their own swath's training gps_time span. A spline cannot extrapolate, so this attributes a large-block blow-up rather than leaving it mysterious
columns.skill: 1 - var(route)/var(base) on held-out cells. Positive = better than doing nothing. NEGATIVE MEANS IT INJECTS ERROR

headline: 100 m: ours skill +0.160 vs delong +0.444; 200 m: ours skill +0.142 vs delong +0.384; 400 m: ours skill +0.087 vs delong +0.283
